text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated timeout rate observed in prod: inference-gateway - p95->p99 spike, 5xx/timeouts up ~7% across customer-facing routes. Auto-page sent to #incidents.

sanjay: oncall here, investigating. which routes? any correlating deploys? :eyes:

katie: saw this right after a deploy rolled to 100% from the release pipeline. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat-stream. Region: us-west-2 mostly. Canary looked OK for ~10m then p99 jumped.

ryan: that was my deploy — release id d7f4c9b -> rollout 100% at ~19:12. I can start rollback if we decide.

maria: quick metrics snippet from dashboards:
```
service: inference-gateway
baseline p99: 1.1s
current p99: 6.8s
5xx rate: 0.7% -> 7.4%
errors mostly: gateway_timeout / upstream_read_timeout
```

beth: customer impact: several PLG customers reported cold calls timing out; one enterprise reported degraded UX but no data loss. I've drafted a status note for affected customers, holding send until we have mitigation.

sanjay: plan: 1) throttle rollout / route traffic away from new version 2) if not improving in 3m, rollback to v1.23.4 3) notify customers. Who's executing 1?

katie: I can push traffic to previous revision via router. Executing: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/reload-route -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","target":"v1.23.4"}'` — running now.

deploy-bot: router change accepted, 65% traffic shifted to v1.23.4, 35% still on d7f4c9b.

sanjay: running quick health checks: `curl -s https://gateway/probe/health | jq .` — showing some upstream 502/504s still. folks run `kubectl logs -n prod inference-gateway-... | tail -n 80` and grep for timeout

ryan: grabbing logs, seeing a pattern: long waits on kv-cache lookups and flapping upstream keepalives. snippet:
```
WARN  gateway/route.go: client timeout waiting for upstream: context deadline exceeded
ERROR runtime/pool.go: connection reset by peer while muxing
```

maria: can we spin up a dedicated pool fallback? I can flip route policy to prefer dedicated-pool for heavy routes.

katie: doing dedicated fallback now -> `opsctl route set-policy inference-gateway --prefer dedicated-pool`  (applied)

deploy-bot: traffic policy updated: preferred pool = dedicated-pool. Immediate effect: ~50% of requests rerouted within 40s.

sanjay: monitoring after routing change... p99 dropped to 2.3s but 5xx still elevated at ~3.2%.

beth: customers: recommend sending interim note: "we are mitigating an ongoing latency issue, working on rollback; interim routing changes applied." ready to send on your go.

sanjay: give us one more minute to see if rollback is needed.

katie: rollback to v1.23.4 initiated: `./infra/rollback --service inference-gateway --to v1.23.4 --reason "p99 timeout regression post-deploy"`

deploy-bot: rollback job started (job id: rb-1965432101). Progress: draining pods on d7f4c9b, scaling up v1.23.4.

sanjay: ack. I'm watching traces. also toggled KV cache TTL to 30s to reduce backend pressure: `featureflag kv-cache-short-ttl on`.

ryan: looking into commit diff now — suspicious change in connection pooling + new runtime header batching in d7f4c9b.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. All traffic to v1.23.4. New assignment: inference-gateway @ v1.23.4.

maria: metrics post-rollback: p99 -> 1.25s, 5xx -> 0.4% (near baseline). Latency tail improved quickly.

sanjay: confirmed. marking incident as mitigated. leaving monitoring window open for 30m. paging handoff to oncall-2 for observation.

oncall-2: ack — i'll monitor for 30m and will escalate if >2% 5xx or p99 >2s sustained.

beth: sending customer interim note now.

katie: created a follow-up ticket: INF-4921 "postmortem: deploy d7f4c9b caused timeout regression via connection-pooling change" assigned to runtime team. cc: release owner (ryan), infra.

sanjay: nice work team. action items: 1) postmortem with root cause and revert criteria 2) add canary duration + traffic ramp guard 3) add automatic rollback threshold for p99/5xx. I'll triage after monitoring window.

incident-bot: Incident closed -> mitigated by rollback and routing fallback. Tags: rollback, routing-fallback, oncall-handoff, customer-notified.

oncall-2: leaving a note for handoff to next shift in ~30m. :white_check_mark:
